paths.title: Frontend, UI & UX Design
paths.description: Build AI-generated interfaces that are coherent, responsive, accessible, state-complete, and grounded in a design system.

lessons.title: Design before styling
lessons.principle: A polished screen can still have a broken information hierarchy.
lessons.practice: Define user goals, content hierarchy, primary actions, and states before visual decoration.

lessons.title: Use a design system
lessons.principle: Ad hoc component generation creates inconsistency.
lessons.practice: Reuse tokens, typography, spacing, colors, controls, and interaction patterns.

lessons.title: Define responsive behavior
lessons.principle: Desktop screenshots do not specify mobile behavior.
lessons.practice: Describe how layout, navigation, content density, and controls adapt across available space.

lessons.title: Design all interaction states
lessons.principle: Controls need more than default appearance.
lessons.practice: Specify hover, focus, active, disabled, loading, success, error, and empty states.

lessons.title: Preserve semantic HTML
lessons.principle: Native semantics improve accessibility and resilience.
lessons.practice: Use buttons for actions, links for navigation, labels for form controls, and landmarks for page structure.

lessons.title: Make keyboard use complete
lessons.principle: Clickable visuals are not enough.
lessons.practice: Ensure all actions are reachable, operable, and visibly focused without a pointer.

lessons.title: Manage focus intentionally
lessons.principle: Dialogs, route changes, errors, and dynamic content can disorient keyboard and screen-reader users.
lessons.practice: Move and restore focus according to the interaction context.

lessons.title: Use clear form validation
lessons.principle: Users need to know what failed and how to fix it.
lessons.practice: Connect field errors to inputs, preserve entered data, and validate authoritatively on the server.

lessons.title: Avoid layout shift
lessons.principle: Late-loading content can move controls under the user.
lessons.practice: Reserve space for media and async content and use stable skeletons when useful.

lessons.title: Design meaningful loading
lessons.principle: Indefinite spinners provide little information.
lessons.practice: Use immediate feedback, progress where knowable, and optimistic UI only when rollback is safe.

lessons.title: Design empty states as onboarding
lessons.principle: An empty product surface should help users begin.
lessons.practice: Explain why the space is empty and present the next useful action.

lessons.title: Respect reduced motion
lessons.principle: Motion should not block or distress users.
lessons.practice: Honor user preferences and avoid unnecessary parallax, flashing, or large movement.

lessons.title: Optimize text readability
lessons.principle: Generated interfaces often overuse tiny muted text.
lessons.practice: Use sufficient contrast, readable line length, clear hierarchy, and scalable text.

lessons.title: Treat errors as product states
lessons.principle: Technical messages rarely help users.
lessons.practice: Translate failures into actionable language without hiding support-relevant context.

lessons.title: Use optimistic UI carefully
lessons.principle: Fast-feeling interfaces can lie when operations fail.
lessons.practice: Apply optimistic updates only when conflicts and rollback are well-defined.

lessons.title: Preserve URL state where useful
lessons.principle: Shareable and restorable application state improves usability.
lessons.practice: Represent navigable selections, filters, or resources in URLs when appropriate.

lessons.title: Test with real content extremes
lessons.principle: Placeholder text hides overflow and density problems.
lessons.practice: Use long names, empty values, large numbers, translated strings, and many items during UI validation.

lessons.title: Avoid generic AI aesthetics
lessons.principle: Repeated gradients, oversized hero text, and decorative clutter can weaken product identity.
lessons.practice: Ground generated designs in the actual brand, audience, content, and product purpose.

lessons.title: Validate visually and functionally
lessons.principle: A DOM that compiles can still render incorrectly.
lessons.practice: Use browser verification across key viewport sizes, interactions, and error states.

lessons.title: Optimize the full journey
lessons.principle: Local component quality does not guarantee a coherent product.
lessons.practice: Review navigation, task completion, recovery, and consistency across the entire user flow.

paths.title: Backend & API Engineering
paths.description: Generate server-side code with explicit contracts, validation, authorization, idempotency, reliability, and operational behavior.

lessons.title: Validate at trust boundaries
lessons.principle: External input is untrusted regardless of client validation.
lessons.practice: Parse and validate request bodies, parameters, headers, files, and external service data on the server.

lessons.title: Separate authentication and authorization
lessons.principle: Knowing who a caller is does not imply what they may do.
lessons.practice: Authenticate identity, then enforce resource- and action-specific authorization.

lessons.title: Use resource ownership checks
lessons.principle: Object-level authorization failures expose other users' data.
lessons.practice: Verify tenant, owner, membership, or policy for every sensitive resource access.

lessons.title: Return meaningful HTTP semantics
lessons.principle: Clients need predictable status behavior.
lessons.practice: Use methods and status codes consistently and include machine-readable error structures.

lessons.title: Design idempotency for retries
lessons.principle: Clients and infrastructure may retry requests.
lessons.practice: Protect create, payment, and side-effecting operations with idempotency mechanisms when repetition is unsafe.

lessons.title: Bound request work
lessons.principle: Long or unbounded requests consume capacity and fail unpredictably.
lessons.practice: Use limits, timeouts, pagination, and background jobs for expensive work.

lessons.title: Protect against N+1 access
lessons.principle: Generated data-fetching code can perform one query per item.
lessons.practice: Batch, join, prefetch, or otherwise bound database calls on list endpoints.

lessons.title: Use transactions for invariants
lessons.principle: Related writes can partially succeed without atomicity.
lessons.practice: Wrap operations that must commit together in a database transaction.

lessons.title: Handle partial external failure
lessons.principle: Third-party APIs can timeout or return inconsistent errors.
lessons.practice: Define retry classes, timeouts, circuit behavior, and compensation for side effects.

lessons.title: Design rate limits
lessons.principle: Public endpoints can be abused even when functionally correct.
lessons.practice: Limit by appropriate identity and operation while returning useful retry information.

lessons.title: Use structured errors
lessons.principle: String-only errors are hard to automate and localize.
lessons.practice: Return stable error codes with safe messages and correlation identifiers.

lessons.title: Avoid leaking internals
lessons.principle: Stack traces and database errors reveal implementation details.
lessons.practice: Log detailed diagnostics server-side and return bounded public errors.

lessons.title: Make pagination deterministic
lessons.principle: Unstable ordering can duplicate or skip results.
lessons.practice: Use explicit stable order and cursor-based pagination where data changes frequently.

lessons.title: Version contracts deliberately
lessons.principle: Clients may outlive a backend deployment.
lessons.practice: Prefer additive changes and introduce explicit versions when compatibility cannot be preserved.

lessons.title: Protect webhook endpoints
lessons.principle: Webhook requests come from outside the trust boundary.
lessons.practice: Verify signatures, timestamps, replay protection, and event idempotency.

lessons.title: Use background jobs safely
lessons.principle: Queues add retry and duplication semantics.
lessons.practice: Make jobs idempotent, observable, bounded, and dead-lettered when repeated failure requires inspection.

lessons.title: Implement graceful shutdown
lessons.principle: Deployments should not abandon accepted work.
lessons.practice: Stop new traffic, drain in-flight requests or jobs, and close resources within a timeout.

lessons.title: Expose liveness and readiness separately
lessons.principle: A running process may not be able to serve traffic.
lessons.practice: Use readiness for required dependencies and liveness for process recovery decisions.

lessons.title: Document API examples
lessons.principle: Contracts are easier to use when examples match the schema.
lessons.practice: Keep representative requests, responses, errors, and authentication examples current.

lessons.title: Test contracts at boundaries
lessons.principle: Backend correctness depends on more than unit logic.
lessons.practice: Add integration tests for validation, permissions, persistence, external adapters, and failure responses.
